explanation.text:
(Pro. 16:1-33)

preparations--schemes.

in man--or literally, "to man," belonging, or pertaining to him.

the answer . . . Lord--The efficient ordering is from God: "Man proposes; God disposes."

bsb.text: The plans of the heart belong to man, but the reply of the tongue is from the LORD.

explanation.text:
clean--or, "faultless."

weigheth--or, "tries," "judges," implying that they are faulty (Pro 21:2; Pro 24:12).

bsb.text: All a man’s ways are pure in his own eyes, but his motives are weighed out by the LORD.

explanation.text: (Compare Margin). Rely on God for success to your lawful purposes.

bsb.text: Commit your works to the LORD and your plans will be achieved.

explanation.text: for himself--"for its answer," or "purpose," that is, according to God's plan; the wicked are for the day of evil (Psa 49:5; Jer 17:18); sinning and suffering answer to each other, are indissolubly united.

bsb.text: The LORD has made everything for His purpose—even the wicked for the day of disaster.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 3:32).

bsb.text: Everyone who is proud in heart is detestable to the LORD; be assured that he will not go unpunished.

explanation.text:
By mercy and truth--that is, God's (Psa 85:10); He effects the atonement, or covering of sin; and the principles of true piety incline men to depart from evil; or, "mercy" and "truth" may be man's, indicative of the gracious tempers which work instrumentally in procuring pardon.

purged--expiated (as in Lev 16:33; Isa 27:9, Hebrew).

bsb.text: By loving devotion and faithfulness iniquity is atoned for, and by the fear of the LORD one turns aside from evil.

explanation.text: Persecutions, of course, excepted.

bsb.text: When a man’s ways please the LORD, He makes even the man’s enemies live at peace with him.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 15:6, Pro 15:16-17).

bsb.text: Better a little with righteousness than great gain with injustice.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 16:3).

directeth--establisheth.

bsb.text: A man’s heart plans his course, but the LORD determines his steps.

explanation.text: The last clause depends on the first, expressing the importance of equity in decisions, so authoritative.

bsb.text: A divine verdict is on the lips of a king; his mouth must not betray justice.

explanation.text: are the Lord's . . . his work--that is, what He has ordered, and hence should be observed by men.

bsb.text: Honest scales and balances are from the LORD; all the weights in the bag are His concern.

explanation.text: Rulers are rightly expected, by their position, to hate evil; for their power is sustained by righteousness.

bsb.text: Wicked behavior is detestable for kings, for a throne is established through righteousness.

explanation.text: A specification of the general sentiment of Pro 16:12.

bsb.text: Righteous lips are a king’s delight, and he who speaks honestly is beloved.

explanation.text: This wrath, so terrible and certain, like messengers of death (Kg1 2:25), can be appeased by the wise.

bsb.text: The wrath of a king is a messenger of death, but a wise man will pacify it.

explanation.text:
light of . . . countenance--favor (Psa 4:6).

life--preserves it, or gives blessings which make it valuable.

the latter rain--fell just before harvest and matured the crop; hence specially valuable (Deu 11:14).

bsb.text: When a king’s face brightens, there is life; his favor is like a rain cloud in spring.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 3:16; Pro 4:5).

bsb.text: How much better to acquire wisdom than gold! To gain understanding is more desirable than silver.

explanation.text:
The highway--A common, plain road represents the habitual course of the righteous in departing from evil.

keepeth--observes.

bsb.text: The highway of the upright leads away from evil; he who guards his way protects his life.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 15:33). Haughtiness and pride imply self-confidence which produces carelessness, and hence

a fall--literally, "sliding."

bsb.text: Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.

explanation.text: divide the spoil--that is, conquer. Avoid the society of the proud (Jam 4:6).

bsb.text: It is better to be lowly in spirit among the humble than to divide the spoil with the proud.

explanation.text:
handleth a matter--wisely considers "the word," that is, of God (compare Pro 13:13).

trusteth--(Compare Psa 2:12; Psa 118:8-9).

bsb.text: Whoever heeds instruction will find success, and blessed is he who trusts in the LORD.

explanation.text:
wise in heart--who rightly consider duty.

sweetness of the lips--eloquent discourse, persuades and instructs others.

bsb.text: The wise in heart are called discerning, and pleasant speech promotes instruction.

explanation.text: Understanding--or, "discretion," is a constant source of blessing (Pro 13:14), benefiting others; but fools' best efforts are folly.

bsb.text: Understanding is a fountain of life to its possessor, but the discipline of fools is folly.

explanation.text: The heart is the source of wisdom flowing from the mouth.

bsb.text: The heart of the wise man instructs his mouth and adds persuasiveness to his lips.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 15:26). Gentle, kind words, by soothing the mind, give the body health.

bsb.text: Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul and healing to the bones.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 14:2).

bsb.text: There is a way that seems right to a man, but its end is the way of death.

explanation.text: Diligence is a duty due to one's self, for his wants require labor.

bsb.text: A worker’s appetite works for him because his hunger drives him onward.

explanation.text:
ungodly man--(Compare Pro 6:12).

diggeth up evil--labors for it.

in his lips . . . fire--His words are calumniating (Jam 3:6).

bsb.text: A worthless man digs up evil, and his speech is like a scorching fire.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 6:14; Pro 10:31).

whisperer--prater, talebearer (Pro 18:8; Pro 26:20).

bsb.text: A perverse man spreads dissension, and a gossip divides close friends.

explanation.text:
violent man--or, "man of mischief" (Pro 3:31).

enticeth-- (Pro 1:10).

bsb.text: A violent man entices his neighbor and leads him down a path that is not good.

explanation.text:
He shutteth his eyes--denoting deep thought (Psa 64:6).

moving his lips--or, "biting his lips"--a determined purpose (Pro 6:13).

bsb.text: He who winks his eye devises perversity; he who purses his lips is bent on evil.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 20:29).

if--or, which may be supplied properly, or without it the sense is as in Pro 3:16; Pro 4:10, that piety is blessed with long life.

bsb.text: Gray hair is a crown of glory; it is attained along the path of righteousness.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 14:29).

taketh a city--that is, by fighting.

bsb.text: He who is slow to anger is better than a warrior, and he who controls his temper is greater than one who captures a city.

explanation.text:
Seemingly the most fortuitous events are ordered by God.

bsb.text: The lot is cast into the lap, but its every decision is from the LORD.
